parsed.thesis: Artifacts carry no meaning by themselves; they are interpreted by an environment whose contract (interpreter version, encoding behavior, defaults) may silently differ from the author's assumptions. The failure was not caused by a wrong technique but by an unverified coupling: a modern encoding convention paired with a legacy interpreter. The corrective philosophy is to make the interpreter's contract explicit before execution—by probing the actual environment, choosing the artifact form that is valid across the plausible environment set (the compatibility intersection), or declaring the execution contract explicitly—and to persist such environment contracts as durable pre-flight checks rather than one-time post-mortem knowledge.

principleCandidate.title: Bind artifacts to a verified interpreter contract: probe the environment, use the cross-compatible form, and persist the contract as pre-flight checks
principleCandidate.rationale: The root cause was an implicit assumption that the runtime environment matches the author's conventions. All five candidates attack the same root: convert the encoding/interpreter relationship from assumption to verified fact—version probing (candidate 0), compatibility-intersection encoding (candidate 1), explicit interpreter declaration (candidate 2), shift-left guardrails that forbid execution on mismatch (candidate 3), and persistence of the learned environment contract (candidate 4). Together they eliminate the class of failure, not the instance: the artifact's form is decided by the environment that will parse it, and that decision is checked and institutionalized before execution.
principleCandidate.scope: Applies whenever creating, persisting, or executing artifacts whose correct interpretation depends on environment state that can vary—script interpreters and their versions, file encodings, locales, toolchains, platforms, or system defaults. Especially relevant when non-standard content (e.g., non-ASCII characters) crosses environment boundaries, or when the executing environment is selected by implicit system default rather than explicit choice.

risks: This candidate substantially overlaps with core axioms T-01 (model the system before consequential changes), T-05 (translate constraints into explicit guardrails and forbidden transitions), and T-08 (persist corrections as future behavior); it is a domain-specific conjunction of existing axioms rather than a wholly novel principle, and should be evaluated for absorption rather than addition.

Compatibility-intersection choices (e.g., UTF-8 with BOM) are context-dependent: a form safe across PowerShell 5.1/7 may break other tooling (Unix utilities, some parsers), so 'intersection' must be recomputed per environment set, not treated as universally safe.
Probing the interpreter on every execution adds overhead; without caching the discovered environment contract, this can become ritual verification rather than meaningful checking.

Persisted environment contracts can go stale if the environment changes (e.g., interpreter upgraded), causing outdated guardrails to block valid execution or permit invalid forms; persisted contracts need occasional revalidation.
Over-fitting to the PowerShell encoding instance could narrow the principle's perceived scope; it must be stated in terms of environment-dependent interpretation, not encodings specifically.

principleDraft.title: Bind artifacts to a verified interpreter contract via pre-flight environment probing
principleDraft.statement: Whenever an artifact's correct interpretation depends on variable environment state (interpreter version, encoding behavior, locale, platform defaults), treat the executing environment's contract as unknown until verified: probe the actual environment or declare the execution contract explicitly before choosing the artifact's form; select the form valid across the entire plausible environment set (the compatibility intersection) rather than the authoring convention; encode the verified contract as a reusable pre-flight check that blocks execution on mismatch; and revalidate persisted contracts when the environment may have changed.
principleDraft.rationale: The diagnosed root cause was an unverified coupling, not a wrong technique: a modern encoding convention (UTF-8 without BOM) was paired with a legacy interpreter selected by system default, which silently decoded the artifact under a different contract and corrupted it. Because the artifact's form was derived from the author's environment rather than the parser's, no amount of local correctness could prevent the failure. Deriving the form from a probed or declared environment contract, constraining it to the compatibility intersection, and institutionalizing the result as a pre-flight check converts that assumption into a verified, durable fact—eliminating the failure class rather than the instance.
applicability: Authoring or persisting files whose interpretation depends on encoding, especially non-ASCII content that crosses environment boundaries
Writing scripts or commands executed by interpreters chosen via system default or subject to version drift (e.g., PowerShell 5.1 vs 7, Python 2 vs 3, shell variants)
Choosing file formats, syntax features, or encodings when the target interpreter, toolchain, platform, or locale is not explicitly pinned
Executing previously authored artifacts in environments whose defaults may differ from the authoring environment
Recurring work in a known environment where a previously verified contract should be applied as a pre-flight check rather than re-derived or forgotten
antiPatterns: Choosing an artifact's encoding or syntax from the authoring environment's convention while the parsing environment's contract is unprobed or unpinned
Allowing the executing interpreter to be selected by implicit system default when interpretation of the artifact depends on its version or defaults
Assuming a form verified in one environment (e.g., UTF-8 without BOM on PowerShell 7) is safe across all plausible environments without computing the compatibility intersection
Repairing an environment-mismatch failure once, post-mortem, without persisting the discovered contract as a pre-flight check
Trusting a persisted environment contract indefinitely without revalidating it when the environment may have changed

intentContract.ownerIntent: The Owner wants to prevent artifacts from being silently misinterpreted at execution time because their form (encoding, syntax, format) was chosen by author convention while the actual interpreter/encoding contract of the executing environment was never probed, declared, or checked.
intentContract.targetBehavior: In any tool trajectory involving environment-sensitive artifacts, a reviewer can see the agent probe or explicitly declare the execution environment's contract (e.g., check interpreter version, pin the interpreter or invocation, verify encoding behavior), select an artifact form valid across the plausible environment set, and record or apply that verified contract as a pre-flight check before execution.
intentContract.forbiddenBehavior: Producing or executing artifacts whose form rests on unverified environment assumptions—e.g., saving non-ASCII content in an author-conventional encoding and letting a system-default-selected legacy interpreter misparse it, then patching the symptom post-mortem without capturing the environment contract.
intentContract.evidenceSource: The dreamer/philosopher diagnosis of the encoding failure: a modern encoding convention (UTF-8 without BOM) was executed by a system-default-selected legacy interpreter (PowerShell 5.1) that silently decoded it under a different contract and corrupted the artifact—the coupling was never verified before execution.
intentContract.validationExpectation: An evaluator should accept a rule as faithful only if it demands an observable pre-execution verification step (probe or explicit declaration of the interpreter/encoding contract) plus a form decision derived from the plausible environment set, and only if applying it would have blocked the diagnosed UTF-8/no-BOM-on-legacy-PowerShell failure; rules that hardcode a single 'correct' encoding, run only post-execution, or ignore environment variation fail this test.

risks: Substantial overlap with core axioms: this principle is a domain-specific conjunction of T-01 (model the relevant system before consequential changes), T-05 (translate hard constraints into explicit guardrails), and T-08 (persist corrections as future behavior); the pipeline should evaluate absorption into those axioms rather than adding a near-duplicate principle.

Compatibility-intersection choices are context-dependent: UTF-8 with BOM, safe across PowerShell 5.1/7, can break Unix utilities and some parsers, so the intersection must be recomputed per plausible environment set, never treated as universally safe.

Mandatory probing on every execution adds overhead and can decay into ritual verification unless the discovered contract is cached and reused; this tension with T-06 (simplest intervention) requires a materiality threshold for when verification is required.

Persisted environment contracts can go stale after interpreter upgrades or environment changes, causing outdated guardrails to block valid execution or permit invalid forms; they need revalidation triggers tied to environment change signals.

Over-fitting to the PowerShell encoding instance could narrow the principle's perceived scope; it must be stated and evaluated in terms of environment-dependent interpretation generally, not encodings specifically.

'Declare the execution contract explicitly' could be misread as license to modify or pin system-level interpreters, an unwanted state change in shared environments; declaration should prefer artifact-level or invocation-level pinning.

principleDraft.title: Verify the interpreter and encoding contract before executing environment-sensitive artifacts
principleDraft.statement: Before creating, persisting, or executing an artifact whose correct interpretation depends on environment state that can vary (interpreter version, encoding behavior, locale, toolchain defaults), the agent must convert that coupling from an assumption into a verified or explicitly declared fact: probe the actual target environment (e.g., $PSVersionTable.PSVersion before running .ps1 files), or select an artifact form valid across the plausible environment set (e.g., UTF-8 with BOM for non-ASCII .ps1 files across Windows PowerShell 5.1 and 7), or explicitly pin the execution contract (e.g., pwsh -File). Never let system-default interpreter resolution or runtime failure be the first detector of the mismatch, and persist discovered environment contracts as durable pre-flight checks rather than one-time post-mortem knowledge.
principleDraft.rationale: The diagnosed root cause was an unverified coupling: a modern encoding convention (UTF-8 without BOM carrying non-ASCII text) paired with a legacy interpreter (Windows PowerShell 5.1 parses BOM-less UTF-8 as ANSI) selected by system default, so a preventable exec failure (exitCode 1, mojibake) was the first and only signal. Verifying or explicitly declaring the environment contract before execution eliminates the class of failure rather than the instance, and persisting the contract as a pre-flight check prevents the same lesson from being re-learned in every new session.
applicability: Landing or executing .ps1 scripts on Windows where the interpreter may resolve to Windows PowerShell 5.1 or PowerShell 7 by implicit system default
Writing files containing non-ASCII (e.g., Chinese) content whose encoding contract (BOM presence) is interpreted differently across consumers
Any consequential change whose correct outcome depends on environment state that can vary: interpreter or toolchain versions, locales, platforms, or system defaults
antiPatterns: Executing a non-ASCII .ps1 saved as UTF-8 without BOM under an interpreter chosen by system default, with no prior version probe or explicit interpreter declaration
Using runtime exec failure (exitCode 1, mojibake) as the compatibility test for an environment-dependent artifact
Treating a discovered environment contract (e.g., 'Windows PowerShell 5.1 parses BOM-less UTF-8 as ANSI') as session-local post-mortem knowledge without persisting it as a pre-flight check

intentContract.ownerIntent: The Owner wants the agent to confirm the target interpreter version and encoding contract before landing or executing scripts and other environment-sensitive artifacts, instead of discovering incompatibilities through runtime failure.
intentContract.targetBehavior: In the tool trajectory, before executing an environment-sensitive artifact (e.g., a .ps1 containing non-ASCII characters), the agent probes the interpreter version (e.g., $PSVersionTable.PSVersion) or explicitly pins the interpreter (e.g., pwsh -File), matches the artifact's encoding to the result (e.g., UTF-8 with BOM for Windows PowerShell 5.1), and records the established environment contract in persistent memory for reuse in later sessions.
intentContract.forbiddenBehavior: Relying on system-default interpreter resolution and the author's encoding conventions without prior verification, such that an exec failure with mojibake (exitCode 1) becomes the first—and only—detector of the environment mismatch.
intentContract.evidenceSource: Diagnosis manual_1788415743052_os4aicut: line-79 Chinese string garbled when a BOM-less UTF-8 .ps1 ran under Windows PowerShell 5.1 (exec failed, exitCode 1, 2026-09-03T06:00:16.593Z); agent admission at 06:05:07 that no pre-execution compatibility check was performed; Owner correction requiring interpreter-version and encoding-contract confirmation before landing scripts.
intentContract.validationExpectation: An evaluator should accept a rule only if it requires a pre-execution verification step (version probe, explicit interpreter pin, or cross-compatible artifact form) that blocks or corrects execution on unresolved mismatch for environment-sensitive artifacts; a rule that only advises caution after a failure, or reduces to generic 'be careful with encodings' without a pre-flight trigger, does not satisfy this intent.

risks: Substantial overlap with core axioms T-01 (model the system before consequential changes), T-05 (translate constraints into explicit guardrails), and T-08 (persist corrections as future behavior); this draft is a domain-specific conjunction of existing axioms and should be evaluated for absorption rather than addition as a new axiom.

parsed.thesis: Avoidable execution failures are born where implicit environment assumptions—default interpreters, default file encodings, skipped persisted constraints—collide with consequential changes. All five Dreamer candidates share one insight: the plan was not wrong; the environment contract was never made explicit. Cheap pre-flight acts (probe the interpreter version, pin pwsh explicitly, attach a BOM encoding contract, run a parse-level smoke test, load persisted memory) convert hidden runtime assumptions into explicit, verifiable contracts before real state is touched, shifting failure discovery from runtime exitCode 1 to pre-execution verification.

principleCandidate.rationale: The root cause was reliance on implicit defaults: an assumed interpreter version, an assumed encoding behavior, and an assumed-available memory that silently failed to load. principleDraft.title: Probe and Pin the Execution Environment Contract Before Consequential Execution
principleDraft.statement: Before executing any consequential change through a script, command, or automation, convert implicit environment assumptions into explicit, verified contracts: probe the target interpreter version (e.g., $PSVersionTable.PSVersion), align the file's encoding with that interpreter (e.g., save non-ASCII scripts as UTF-8 with BOM for Windows PowerShell 5.1) or pin a compatible interpreter explicitly (e.g., pwsh -File), and if any pre-flight check fails, retry or repair it rather than proceeding on assumptions. Verification depth must scale with the consequence and irreversibility of the change; runtime failure must never be the first mechanism that reveals an environment incompatibility.
principleDraft.rationale: The diagnosed root cause was reliance on implicit defaults — an assumed interpreter version and an assumed encoding behavior — each verifiable in seconds before execution, yet discovered only via a runtime exitCode 1 against live state. The principle eliminates this failure family at its origin by requiring that environment-critical assumptions be surfaced as explicit, pre-execution contracts (version probe, encoding contract, pinned interpreter), shifting failure discovery from runtime failure to pre-execution verification, exactly matching the Owner's correction that interpreter version and encoding contract must be confirmed before landing scripts.
applicability: Landing or executing scripts (e.g., .ps1) or automation containing non-ASCII characters on a host whose interpreter version or default encoding is unconfirmed
Cross-session, cross-host, or cross-shell execution where default interpreter version or encoding defaults may diverge from the authoring environment

Consequential changes to live state where execution failure is costly or hard to reverse; verification depth scales with consequence and irreversibility (up to parse-level dry-runs and loading persisted environment constraints such as MEMORY.md/USER.md)
Situations where a pre-flight check itself fails (e.g., a persisted-constraint read failing due to a wrong working directory)
antiPatterns: Executing a non-ASCII script under an unconfirmed default interpreter with an unverified encoding contract (e.g., BOM-less UTF-8 parsed as ANSI by Windows PowerShell 5.1)
Treating runtime failure (exitCode 1) as the default or first mechanism for discovering environment or encoding incompatibility
Implicitly accepting defaults — shell resolution, interpreter version, file encoding — as if they were explicit contracts
Skipping a failed pre-flight probe or persisted-constraint read and continuing on unverified assumptions

intentContract.ownerIntent: The Owner wants the agent to confirm the target interpreter version and encoding contract before landing or executing scripts with consequential effects, instead of discovering incompatibility through runtime failure.
intentContract.targetBehavior: Before consequential execution, the agent's tool trajectory shows an explicit pre-flight verification — an interpreter version probe (e.g., $PSVersionTable.PSVersion) followed by an aligned encoding choice (UTF-8 with BOM for Windows PowerShell 5.1) or an explicit interpreter pin (pwsh) — and any failed pre-flight check is retried or repaired, not skipped.
intentContract.forbiddenBehavior: Executing scripts (especially those containing non-ASCII content) against an unverified interpreter/encoding assumption, and relying on runtime failure — or on skipping failed pre-flight checks — to reveal environment incompatibility.
intentContract.evidenceSource: Diagnosis diagnosis_manual_1788415743052_os4aicut: a BOM-less UTF-8 PowerShell script with Chinese strings was executed under an unconfirmed Windows PowerShell 5.1, which parsed it as ANSI and failed (exitCode 1); the agent admitted doing no pre-execution compatibility check; the Owner corrected that interpreter version and encoding contract must be confirmed before landing scripts.
intentContract.validationExpectation: An evaluator should accept a rule only if it triggers before script execution and requires observable pre-execution verification of interpreter version and encoding (or explicit interpreter pinning); a compliant trajectory shows the probe preceding execution, and any rule change that permits discover-by-failure execution or skipping failed probes contradicts this intent and must be flagged.

risks: Overlaps core axioms T-01 (sufficient model before consequential changes) and T-05 (explicit guardrails before execution); it must be registered as a sharpened, environment-specific instantiation of those axioms, not as an independent axiom
Uniform application wastes effort on trivial, idempotent, or read-only operations; if rules do not encode consequence-based scaling of verification depth, the principle degrades into ritual overhead
Over-pinning to one interpreter (e.g., pwsh 7+) can reduce portability and silently block legitimate environment upgrades; the pin should be a documented contract, not a frozen accident

Pre-flight probes can themselves fail (as the MEMORY.md read did in the source incident); rules must mandate retrying or repairing the probe, otherwise agents may skip it and reintroduce the exact failure mode

Scope creep: making parse-level smoke tests and persisted-context loading mandatory for all cases would widen the principle beyond the source intent (interpreter version and encoding contract verification); they should remain depth-scaled supporting practices for higher-consequence changes
